text: Hello everyone, it's me again.In the last lesson, we practiced listening together, and learned how to give directions and show locations.Today, we will continue to talk about locations, and describe them in our writing.Do you remember this dialogue we learned in 7A?The removal man David is asking Mrs.Lee where he should put the furniture in her new flat.How does Mrs.Lee tell him the accurate locations?By using prepositions.And we know then how the room might look like.From the dialogue, we learned to use prepositions to describe the positions of things in a room.In today's lesson, we will continue to learn how to describe a room.As we know, in the story Blind Man and Eyes in Fire drama, the kind manager led John personally to his room.On the way, she introduced the important places on the floor.What did she do then before she left?She described John's room to him.How would she introduce the room to a person who couldn't see?Yes, she would mainly introduce the furniture and facilities to John.A hotel room usually consists of a single room with a private bathroom.So what can we usually find in a hotel room?Bed, table, cupboard, what else?Have a look at the picture below.Here are the things in John's room.Can you name them in English?Complete task one on your worksheet please.Let's check the answers.Number one, it's a refrigerator.Number two, it's a cupboard.Number three, it's not a sofa, but an armchair.As the name suggests, it has sides that support your arms.What about number four and five?They are bathroom and window.Number six is a table.We can also call it a coffee table.Number seven is a TV set.It looks a little bit out of date.Number eight and nine are bed and telephone.Number ten is a table.We often call it night table or nightstand because it's usually kept at the side of the bed.Where are these things located?Let's look at John's room.This is a floor plan showing a top-down view of the room.Your view is from above, looking down at the top.The manager and John are standing near the door.How many things can you see on their right?Six, what are they?They are the bed, the night table, the armchair, the coffee table, the telephone and the TV set.They are all on the right side of the door.What prepositions will you use to show their locations?Let's have a look.Where is the night table?It's beside or next to the bed.Where is the coffee table?It's opposite the bed.Are there any other ways to describe where it is?Good.It is between the TV set and the armchair.What about the telephone?Where is it?It is on the coffee table.Have a look at the coffee table, the telephone and the armchair.Are they in the middle of the room?No, they are in the corner on our right side.So, we say they are in the right hand corner.Read after me.In the right hand corner.Now, can you use the information above to describe the things on the right of the room?Think about it.Kristina, can you share your answers with us?Okay, the bed is on the right of the door.The night table is beside it.The coffee table is in front of the bed.The TV set is next to it.The armchair is near the table in the right hand corner.The telephone is on the table.Thank you.Now, let's have a look at how the manager describes this part to John.Read and compare.What are the differences between these two paragraphs?Do you have any ideas, Andrew?Well, I noticed that Kristina began all her sentences with nouns, while the manager started with prepositional phrases, and the manager used there is to talk about an item.Good point.Also, to avoid repetition, she uses you will find instead of there is sometimes.We are used to saying something is somewhere, like what we have learned from the text in 7A.But, we can also describe the locations by putting the phrases about places at the beginning.Think about the question.Why did the manager describe like this?I think it is because John is blind.The locations are very important to him.Yes, we can emphasize the location by putting the preposition at the beginning.And people tend to put new information at the end of a sentence.This will help you focus your attention on the new information.In our text, it is the furniture item.In writing, putting new information at the end links sentences together more tightly and produces a text that is easier to read.Look at the arrows here.The manager described the items in a very clear order, didn't she?In this example, we can see the manager gave a better picture of where the things are.Then, how would the manager describe to John the things on the left?Can you have a try?Describe the things on the left side of the room with the words in the box.Use the sentence pattern you have just learned.It's task two on your worksheet.And people tend to put new information at the beginning.I think that's enough to express the focus on the space.好,在门的左边,有一个沙发,在沙发的旁边,你会找到一个洗手间,在房间的左手边,你会找到一个冰箱,还有一个窗户在上面,在沙发的左手边,你会找到一个冰箱,在沙发的左手边,你会找到一个冰箱,Thank you!The order is clear, the prepositions are all correct.Well done!Let's put the two parts he have varied sentence patterns?YesGood job, Andrew!This is a good piece of writing, but a little boring, right?Then how can we make it more interesting?Here is an example.When the writer writes about the windows in the room,What details does he give about the windows?We can find the word big and the phrase as tall as doors.And because of the big windows, the room is very bright.With what?Yes, sunlight.Therefore, the room glows like a jewel box.Besides, we can see rainbows on the yellow walls and green carpet.That shows the room is really colorful.The size and the colors are related to our sense of sight.We call them sensory details.They help make the picture more vivid and the writing more interesting.More examples for you.In the corner of the living room, there is a bookshelf full of books.It makes the room seem warmer.On the coffee table, there is a duck-shaped basket.There is always much fruit in it.The fruit is scented and smells fresh.The writer describes a special feature by adding sensory details like what he sees, smells and how he feels.What sensory details can you add for the things and furniture in your room?What can you see, hear, smell or feel?Or maybe taste?I guess it can be useful when you describe your kitchen.Finally, we can write about how we feel about the room.We end our writing by telling readers why the room is so special for us.Here's an example.I like our living room because it is so airy and light.I feel really refreshed in the room.Or we can write about the activities we like to do in the room.For example, the living room might be small, but I like it because it is usually quiet.And I can just lie on the bed and relax, read a book or listen to music.In the end, we can conclude like this.In fact, I like being in the living room better than almost anywhere else.Do you know how to give your favorite room a vivid description now?To sum up, remember the following steps when describing your favorite room.Go through all of these things, and you can't go wrong.Now, you've seen a lot of useful language you can use to talk about your favorite room.Let's put everything together and practice making a long answer.Please.A vivid picture of the room, isn't it?Could you make an answer like this?Practice it at home.Today's homework.Complete your writing my favorite room.Try to use as much language you
